questions.stem: The graph of $y = 2f(x)$ compared to $y = f(x)$ is:

options.text: Stretched vertically by a factor of $2$
Stretched horizontally by a factor of $2$
Compressed vertically by a factor of $2$

questions.explanation: Multiplying $f(x)$ by $2$ doubles every $y$-value, which stretches the graph vertically by a scale factor of $2$.

questions.stem: The point $(4, 7)$ lies on $y = f(x)$. What are the coordinates of the corresponding point on $y = f(x + 3) - 1$?
questions.explanation: $f(x + 3)$ translates the graph $3$ units left, and $-1$ translates it $1$ unit down. So $(4, 7)$ becomes $(4 - 3,\, 7 - 1) = (1, 6)$.

questions.stem: The graph of $y = f(-x)$ is the graph of $y = f(x)$:
questions.explanation: Replacing $x$ with $-x$ reflects the graph in the $y$-axis. Each point $(a, b)$ maps to $(-a, b)$.
